title.en: Geography: India - Location, Relief and Drainage

text.en: Asha traced India's shape on a map. "Mountains in the north, sea on three sides," she said.

India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres. The approximate north–south latitude range of its mainland is 8°04′ N to 37°06′ N. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle. The Standard Meridian is 82.5 degrees east, which gives Indian Standard Time.
India's physical divisions are the Northern Mountains (Himalayas), the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiris, and Anaimudi is the highest peak in South India.
The major Himalayan rivers flow throughout the year, with supplies from rain and, in many headwaters, snow and ice melt. Many peninsular rivers depend more directly on seasonal rainfall. The Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery flow east. The Narmada and Tapi are west-flowing examples.
India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres. The mainland stretches approximately from eight degrees four minutes north to thirty-seven degrees six minutes north.

text.en: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle.

board.text: Standard Meridian

text.en: The standard meridian is eighty-two degrees thirty minutes east. Indian Standard Time is five hours thirty minutes ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.

board.text: Himalayas

text.en: India's physical divisions are the Northern Mountains (Himalayas), the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.

board.text: Western Ghats

text.en: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiris, and Anaimudi is the highest peak in South India.

board.text: peninsular rivers

text.en: The Ganga, Indus and Brahmaputra are major Himalayan river systems. Rain, and snow or ice melt in parts of their basins, help keep their main rivers flowing throughout the year.

board.text: Deccan Plateau

text.en: Many peninsular rivers receive most of their water from rain and vary in flow by season. The Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery flow towards the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada and Tapi are examples of west-flowing rivers.

board.text: Tropic of Cancer

text.en: Latitude measures distance in degrees north or south of the equator. The quoted southern latitude describes the mainland. Indian islands extend farther south.

board.text: Latitude locates places north or south

text.en: Longitude measures angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. India’s longitudes are east of that reference.

board.text: Longitude locates places east or west

text.en: The Tropic of Cancer lies near twenty-three and a half degrees north. On a reference map, trace it across India from west to east.

board.text: The Tropic of Cancer crosses India

text.en: Local solar noon arrives earlier in the east than in the west. India uses one official standard time to coordinate work across longitudes.

board.text: A standard time keeps clocks coordinated

text.en: A plain, plateau and mountain range differ in elevation and slope. These differences affect river direction, soils and settlements.

board.text: Relief describes the shape and height of the land

text.en: Textbook maps distinguish the Greater Himalayas, Lesser Himalayas and Siwalik foothills. The ranges are broadly arranged in belts rather than forming one line.

board.text: The Himalayas include several ranges

text.en: Rivers carry sediment from higher land and deposit it on the plains. Long periods of deposition helped build broad alluvial surfaces.

board.text: The Northern Plains contain river deposits

text.en: Some floodplains receive fresh sediment during floods. Higher surfaces may have older deposits and may flood less often.

board.text: Newer and older alluvium can occur side by side

text.en: Much of the plateau is an ancient rocky landmass. Central highlands and the Deccan Plateau are two useful divisions in a school relief map.

board.text: The peninsular plateau has old rock

text.en: The Western Ghats form a more continuous high edge. Rivers cut through several stretches of the Eastern Ghats, which are less continuous.

board.text: The Ghats edge parts of the plateau

text.en: The Indian Desert has low rainfall, sand dunes and some seasonal streams. The Luni is a well-known river of the region.

board.text: The Thar lies mainly in western Rajasthan

text.en: The western coastal plain is often narrow. The eastern coastal plain is generally broader and includes large river deltas.

board.text: Coastal plains lie between higher land and sea

text.en: Lakshadweep lies in the Arabian Sea and includes coral islands. The Andaman and Nicobar chain lies towards the eastern side of the Bay of Bengal.

board.text: India has island chains on both sides of the peninsula

text.en: Rain falling inside a basin can flow into the same main river or its tributaries. A ridge separating nearby basins is a watershed divide.

board.text: A drainage basin gathers runoff for one river system

text.en: A tributary carries water into a larger river. A distributary is a branch flowing away from a main channel, often near a delta.

board.text: Tributaries join, distributaries branch

text.en: Rivers such as the Sutlej join the wider Indus system. River basins can cross international borders, so the basin is defined by terrain rather than by a political map.

board.text: The Indus system includes several Himalayan tributaries

text.en: The Ganga meets tributaries such as the Yamuna. Its river system helps drain large parts of northern India on its way towards the Bay of Bengal.

board.text: The Ganga drains a broad plain

text.en: The Brahmaputra enters northeastern India and passes through Assam. It continues into Bangladesh and joins the wider delta system.

board.text: The Brahmaputra turns through the northeast

text.en: The Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery reach the Bay of Bengal. Several build substantial deltas near the coast.

board.text: Several major rivers cross the peninsula eastwards

text.en: Both rivers follow broadly westward valleys and enter the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat. Other smaller west-flowing rivers also exist.

board.text: Narmada and Tapi drain westwards

text.en: A delta can form where sediment builds outward at a mouth. An estuary is a tidal meeting place of river water and seawater.

board.text: A delta and an estuary have different forms

text.en: A river fed mainly by rain can swell during the wet season and diminish in dry months. Basin size, stored water and local conditions also affect its flow.

board.text: Season affects river flow

text.en: Start at the high land, follow a river downstream, then identify its mouth. Look for connections between slope, river direction and coastal features.

problem.en: Why is solar noon earlier at a place farther east, even when official clocks agree?

text.en: Earth’s rotation brings eastern places towards the Sun first.
The two places can still follow the same standard time.

why.en: A shared official time is used for coordination.

problem.en: A smaller river flows into the Ganga. Is it a tributary or distributary?

text.en: Its water joins the larger river.

why.en: The direction of the connection is towards the main river.

text.en: It is a tributary.

why.en: A distributary branches away from a main channel.

problem.en: Which seas receive the Godavari and Narmada respectively?

text.en: Follow the Godavari east to the Bay of Bengal.

why.en: It is one of the major east-flowing peninsular rivers.

text.en: Follow the Narmada west towards the Arabian Sea.

why.en: Its valley takes it towards India’s western coast.

prompt.en: A friend says The Narmada flows into the Bay of Bengal. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It flows west into the Arabian Sea.

points.en: Physical divisions: mountains, plains, plateau, desert, coast, islands.
Major Himalayan rivers flow throughout the year.
Many peninsular rivers vary in flow with seasonal rainfall.
